summary: The agent writes a driver whose acquisition loop exits only when terminal_success is at least eight; the downstream plan-building tail follows the loop.
The agent issues the launch command for that driver. This anchor is a command, not proof of successful startup by itself.
Live inspection shows the driver session, qualification already bound, acquisition successes zero, and the downstream plan not yet built.
The agent identifies the counter reset and diagnoses continued waiting in the acquisition loop.
The agent writes a stop-and-inspect script. This is a prepared action; this anchor alone does not prove that it executed.
The agent announces a repair that uses the persistent qualification-stage binding.
The agent writes the revised tail generator; this anchor is not the revised completion-condition implementation itself.
The agent reports the repaired driver running. This is a reported recovery, not proof that the downstream plan or training completed.
